sections.heading: Hesiod's Theogony
paragraphs: This is Hugh G. Evelyn-White's 1914 prose translation of Hesiod's Theogony, the archaic epic recounting the birth of the gods and the establishment of Zeus's rule over the cosmos.

The translation is reproduced verbatim; nothing is modernised, abridged or silently corrected. Evelyn-White's own explanatory footnotes are not part of Hesiod's text and are not reproduced here (see "Known gaps & anomalies").

sections.heading: The edition
paragraphs: Hugh G. Evelyn-White, ed. and trans., Hesiod, the Homeric Hymns and Homerica (Loeb Classical Library, London: William Heinemann Ltd. / New York: The Macmillan Co., 1914). This is the edition that Perseus's TEI transcription of both the Greek text and the English translation of "Theogony" (Θεογονία) is built from.

Citation in this reader follows the Loeb "card" pagination unit that both language witnesses in the source TEI share (a card typically spans 20–40 lines); Hesiod's poems carry no Book-level division in the manuscript or print tradition, so there is no higher citation level to use instead.

sections.heading: Digital source
paragraphs: The machine-readable text is the TEI XML file tlg0020.tlg001.perseus-eng2.xml (CTS URN urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0020.tlg001.perseus-eng2) from the Perseus Digital Library / OpenGreekAndLatin `canonical-greekLit` GitHub repository. It was fetched once and is bundled with the app; nothing is loaded from the network at runtime.

sections.heading: How it was imported
paragraphs:
The importer walks the single translation
as one continuous text stream and cuts it into 32 cards at each marker (there is no

structure to slice on - see "Known gaps & anomalies"). Evelyn-White's own footnotes () are dropped; wrapping is unwrapped, keeping the word. Entities are decoded and runs of whitespace collapsed; the words are otherwise untouched.

sections.heading: Reference scheme
paragraphs: Citation here is by card, matching the companion theogony-grc Greek work card for card. Each card's Division.ref gives the underlying Greek verse line range. Passage.n is "" throughout.

sections.heading: Known gaps & anomalies
paragraphs:
32 translator's footnote(s) were dropped (not Hesiod's text). No

paragraph structure exists in the source, so each card is imported as a single continuous prose block. See the individual anomaly entries above for the full reasoning.
